Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

lose verb

a game

also lose a game

classical

Traupman 44 (vincor, intransitive “lose”)
Andresian p. 20
Vīv. Exerc. 6, 22

vincor, vincī, victus sum

verb, third conjugation, deponent

be beaten, lose

The passive of vincere, the plain classical way to say it and the pair of vincere, win: victus es, you’ve lost. Traupman’s phrases follow.

Other words

  • lūdō superārī — lose a game

    also used · modern · Traupman 44

  • lūdum perdere — lose a game

    also used · modern · Traupman 44

  • cadō, cadere, cecidī, cāsum — fail, lose (a case, a contest)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Inv. 2.57: causā cadere; Andresian p. 20

    Classically “fall” and so “fail”; of losing it is chiefly the lawyers’ causā cadere, lose one’s case.

Examples

  • Victus es. — Aufertō.

    You’ve lost. — Take it, then.Vīv. Exerc. 6

  • sī perdās, ut id ferās aequō animō

    if you lose, take it calmlyVīv. Exerc. 22

See also win, draw, lose.
